subject: Fitqtl/refine qtl increased LOD scores, but no longer significant

messages.author: 3aa42516a58f414a
messages.subject: Fitqtl/refine qtl increased LOD scores, but no longer significant
parts:
Hello Karl,

In running scanone Haley knott on 168 individuals (BC) for one trait there were two QTLs.

chr   pos  lod
AX.171143060   1  9.58 4.51
AX.171105055  16 27.27 3.80

I then looked at scantwo, and saw that there was an interaction on chr01 and chr16.

So I used makeqtl, fitqtl and refineqtl to build a multiple qtl model. What I found was that when putting both QTLs in the model, the LOD score was below the threshold and very low. After refineqtl, the LOD score increased, however was still low. Does this mean that a single QTL model is best?

Thanks,

Gina

Outputs 

fitqtl.cr <- sim.geno(pc_qtl_rm, step=1, n.draws=100, err=0.001)

qtl.cr.L <- makeqtl(fitqtl.cr, chr=c(1, 16),  pos=c(9.578, 27.27))
qtl.cr.L

  QTL object containing imputed genotypes, with 100 imputations. 

      name chr     pos n.gen
Q1   1...@9.6   1  9.5782     2
Q2 1...@27.3  16 27.2720     2

summary(out.L) # gives overall fit of the model

fitqtl summary

Method: multiple imputation 
Model:  normal phenotype
Number of observations : 165 

Full model result
----------------------------------  
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 

       df        SS       MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue(F)
Model   2  154.0487 77.02437 1.380451 3.779577   0.04164369 0.0441213
Error 162 3921.7713 24.20846                                         
Total 164 4075.8201

----------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Fitqtl/refine qtl increased LOD scores, but no longer significant
parts:
It looks the difference is due to using Haley-Knott in scanone but using imputation in the multiple-QTL methods. Try to figure out why the methods are giving such different results.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Fitqtl/refine qtl increased LOD scores, but no longer significant
parts:
If you’re using Haley-Knott, you need the results of calc.genoprob. If you’re using imputation, you need the results of sim.geno. In scanone and fitqtl, etc., you select the method with method=“hk” or =“imp”.

karl
